title: The Octopus Who Escaped Through a Coin Hole 🐙🪙
yt_title: The Octopus Who Escaped Through a Coin Hole 🐙🪙
yt_description:
"That hole is the size of a coin. You'll never fit!" Chuck the crab was very wrong. 🐙
Octopuses have no bones. A 2026 study filmed them squeezing through tiny holes step by step: one arm first, then the other arms, and the head last. (Ollie and Chuck are fictional; the science is real.)

Source: Xin et al. (2026), National University of Singapore, octopus squeezing study (reported by Science News and Smithsonian).

script: Ollie the octopus lives in a glass tank. Up top, there's one tiny hole. Chuck: Ha! That hole is the size of a coin. You'll never fit! Ollie: Watch me. First, Ollie pokes one arm through the hole. Chuck: One arm? Big deal. Then the other arms. And last, his big head squeezes through. Chuck: No way! Where are your bones?! Ollie: Don't have any. Bye, Chuck! Octopuses really do this: no bones, so they push one arm through first, then the rest, and squeeze the head through last. And Chuck? Still in the tank.
